questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.description:
Given a string `s` containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.
An input string is valid if:
1. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets.
2. Open brackets must be closed in the correct order.
Print 'true' if valid, otherwise 'false'.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
questions.description: Given an integer array `nums`, find the subarray with the largest sum, and print its sum.
questions.subject: Algorithms

questions.title: Time Complexity of QuickSort Worst Case
questions.description: What is the worst-case time complexity of standard QuickSort with first element as pivot?
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.explanation: When the array is already sorted or reverse sorted and the first element is picked as pivot, QuickSort produces highly skewed partitions resulting in O(n^2) worst case.

questions.title: Properties of Inorder Traversal in BST
questions.description: Which of the following statements about Binary Search Tree (BST) traversal is always true?
questions.subject: Data Structures

options.text: Preorder traversal yields keys in ascending sorted order
Inorder traversal yields keys in ascending sorted order
Postorder traversal yields keys in descending sorted order
Level order traversal always yields sorted keys

questions.explanation: By definition of a BST, for every node, left subtree < node < right subtree, hence inorder traversal (left, root, right) always visits nodes in non-decreasing sorted order.

questions.title: SQL Primary Key vs Unique Key
questions.description: Select all true differences between a PRIMARY KEY and a UNIQUE constraint in standard relational databases.
questions.subject: Database Systems

options.text: A table can have only one PRIMARY KEY, but multiple UNIQUE constraints.
A PRIMARY KEY column does not permit NULL values, whereas UNIQUE columns may accept NULL.
PRIMARY KEY is always non-clustered index by default in MySQL/SQL Server.
UNIQUE constraints automatically drop foreign keys on update.

questions.explanation: A table is strictly restricted to one primary key and cannot have NULLs. Unique constraints permit multiple definitions per table and allow NULL entries according to SQL standards.

questions.title: ACID Properties in Relational Databases
questions.description: Explain the ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) in database transaction management. Illustrate each property with a real-world banking fund transfer scenario between two bank accounts.
questions.subject: Database Systems
rubricCriteria: Accurate definitions of Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
Realistic fund transfer example showing debit & credit pairing
Clear explanation of rollback on network failure
